newsitem.title: MALAWI: MALAWI GOVERNMENT PLANS SWEEP OF ILLEGAL TRADERS.
newsitem.headline: MALAWI GOVERNMENT PLANS SWEEP OF ILLEGAL TRADERS.

text.p: The Malawian government said on Tuesday it would mount an inspection by the end of this month to "clean up" illegal foreign traders in the country's main trading cities.

The Commerce and Industry Ministry said in a statement it believed there were "many" unscrupulous business people without residential permits who were hiring Malawians without licences to trade for them, local radio reported.
"Those who violate the trade and immigration laws will, among other measures, have their licences withdrawn," the statement said.

The Ministry's Chief Trading Officer, Mayers Mkandawire, told Reuters in a telephone interview that the exercise would involve immigration and local government departments to help sweep illegal traders mainly from West Africa.
"We are (also) likely going to co-opt the police," Mkandawire added.
The planned action entails searches of businesses to check for licences and immigration permits.
